title: cedarbrook-inference-integration-call-notes-2026-03-03
summary: Working notes from kickoff call with Cedarbrook Health on integrating Redwood Private for inference. Focus: data residency, latency SLOs, throughput, and deployment model (VPC vs on-prem). Lots of follow-ups on legal/KMS + infra contacts.
attendees: Dr. Aaron Holt (Cedarbrook - Head of AI)
content:
Call purpose: kickoff for Cedarbrook Health proof-of-concept using Redwood Private deployment. High-level goals: keep PHI on-prem (or in VPC with customer-managed keys), meet 99.9% availability for 99th percentile token latency < 200ms, support peak of ~50 concurrent inference sessions (~200 qps for short prompts).

Notes / discussion points:
- Deployment model
  - Cedarbrook preference: VPC deployment in AWS us-east-1 with customer-managed KMS for key material. Open to on-prem air-gapped if compliance requires, but prefer VPC first.
  - They will need control-plane isolation + audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
- Data residency / PII handling
  - Must ensure no PHI leaves their VPC; any telemetry/metrics must be scrubbed or routed to their logging.
  - Legal asks for Data Processing Addendum + SOC2 attestation; Lina to forward template checklist.
- Performance / SLOs
  - Target p99 token latency < 200ms for models used in triage flows; p50 < 80ms.
  - Throughput: baseline 50 concurrent sessions, burst to 150 for short windows. Expect average request size ~150 tokens.
  - Samir recommended Dedicated GPU pool sizing: 2x A100-equivalent nodes as starting point with autoscale policy for bursts. Victor flagged that quantized Llama-2-13B variants look likely to meet latency.
- Models and quality
  - Cedarbrook pilot will use a specialized triage model + a more capable assistant for clinician notes. Need to validate hallucination/regression on clinical prompts.
  - We should set up eval harness with their prompt set (Priya to share ~100 prompts).
- Security / keys / networking
  - KMS integration: must support customer-managed keys (CMK) in their AWS account. Lina: ask security engineering doc for KMS flow.
  - Networking: Private endpoints, VPC peering or PrivateLink preferred. Priya will provide network CIDR and peering contacts.
- Observability / auditing
  - They require per-request trace ids, token-level cost breakdown for billing, and export of full audit logs to their S3 bucket (encrypted).
  - Redwood Console retention default okay for pilot, but they may need longer retention for audits.
- Compliance / legal
  - Contract redlines expected around data residency and indemnity. Legal will want sample agreement; Victor to share prior customer clause set.

Gotchas / risks called out:
- If we use hosted telemetry by default we may leak metadata; must ensure telemetry opt-out and log redaction are configured before any prod traffic.
- On-prem option adds significant ops time; keep as contingency but scope pilot for VPC.
- Model behavior: clinical hallucination risk — need eval + human-in-loop gating for early pilot.
- Throughput estimate might be low if background batch jobs are run; Priya to confirm expected QPS per service type.

Action items / next steps:
- Priya (Cedarbrook): share network CIDR, peering contact, and sample prompt set (due 2026-03-06).
- Lina (Redwood Security): send KMS integration checklist and telemetry redaction options (due 2026-03-05).
- Samir (Solutions Eng): propose initial Dedicated sizing and cost estimate + quantized model recommendation (draft by 2026-03-07).
- Victor (Platform Eng): export/audit log workflow and S3 export playbook (draft by 2026-03-07).
- Maya (CS): synthesize notes + create Confluence kickoff doc and link to JIRA CS-1284 (by 2026-03-04).
- Legal: provide DPA template and identify sticky clauses (Maya to loop in Legal and expect 1-week turnaround).

Open questions:
- Will Cedarbrook allow outbound metrics collection to Redwood hosted endpoints during pilot? They prefer minimized outbound traffic. Need explicit opt-in.
- Which models are acceptable for clinical data? They may require model vetting and white-listing.
- Do they need HSM-backed keys (HSM in scope or optional)? Lina to clarify with security team.

Notes to self (informal):
- Emphasize telemetry opt-out in the Confluence doc; mark as blocker for any minimal shared telemetry.
- Push for VPC + CMK for initial deployment to avoid on-prem timeline.
- Prepare a short eval checklist focused on hallucination metrics and safety thresholds we can run on their 100 prompts.
- Remember to record cost per 1k tokens differential between quantized 13B and float32 13B for their budget discussion.

Useful links mentioned during call:
- Internal KMS integration doc: github.com/redwood/docs/kms-integration (Samir)
- Export logs playbook (internal): CONF-3241
- Prior similar customer note: users/novusbank-call-notes-integration-sla-2026-02-18.json

Next meeting: schedule follow-up after artifacts received, tentatively week of 2026-03-09.
